# The instrument configuration sections, ported

**38 of 58 groups ported; 20 blocked, each on a named input.** Generated by `scratch/cfg_port_report.py` off `finastro/rules/config_rules.CONFIG_REGISTRY` and `build/astronomy_2027.json`. Nothing on this page is typed: the counts come from the registry, the titles and verdicts are slices of `data/source_2026.html`, and the firing counts come from `fire()`.

These are **not** catalogue-B sections. They live in their own registry, `ConfigGroup.b` is None, and `rules.sections_ported()` cannot see them, so catalogue B's 141/141 is unchanged by this port and means exactly what it meant before.

## The verdict is stated in two elements, and that is the whole trap

A catalogue-B verdict is sliced out of its own section. A configuration verdict is sliced out of **two**: the block's `<h2>` carries the direction and the group heading carries the condition. *Silver — Bullish Configuration* + *Venus Mars Together* is one statement in two halves.

**34 of the 58 group headings state no direction after a dash of their own.** A port that sliced only the group heading — the catalogue-B operation, applied unchanged — would have produced 34 rules with `verdict_text = None`, and every one would have rendered as a blank cell rather than as an error. That is the `family` half-match in a new costume and the fifth instance of the shape.

`finastro/rules/config_catalogue.check_verdict` runs at REGISTRATION, before any rule can fire, and raises `SilentVerdict` on three things: a null verdict under a directional block, a verdict that is not a substring of the document, and a verdict with no attribution. The import fails; it is not a report. The check was written before the first rule, not after.

Result: **36 verdicts come from the block `<h2>`, 22 from the group heading, and none is null.** `tests/test_rule_layer.py` asserts all of that, runs the naive slice as a counterfactual, and checks that the guard actually refuses each of the three cases rather than being decoration.

## The blocked twenty, by input

| input | groups | is it one of the survey's five? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `valence` | **9** | yes |
| `darshan` | **4** | yes |
| `month_system` | **3** | yes |
| `aspect_orb` | **2** | yes |
| `vedha_wheel` | **2** | **no — and not an input the document withholds: a consequence of §12.10** |
| `no_dated_window` | **1** | yes |

`silver-bearish#9` is blocked on two inputs and appears in two rows; the group total is 20, not 21.

* **`valence`** — a benefic/malefic classification of the bodies -- the source selects rows on 'malefic' or 'benefic' and never defines either. The same absence blocks B19, B116 and B117
* **`darshan`** — a first-sighting (darshan / moonrise-as-sighting) computation. B62 is the same computation and is blocked; swe.heliacal_ut ran 9-10 days out against the source's own Venus rise dates
* **`no_dated_window`** — nothing to port: the source prints a title and no dated window, so there is no condition to register a reproduction against
* **`month_system`** — the lunar month system, amanta or purnimanta. The event itself is emitted; NAMING its month is what is open. `month_system_confirmation` in config, and B111
* **`aspect_orb`** — the aspect doctrine -- graha drishti or a degree orb. `aspect_orbs` in config. The layer emits conjunction and opposition only, so a 3rd/10th-house aspect has no series
* **`vedha_wheel`** — a per-planet Nakshtra Vedh wheel for the planet the group names. Mercury's is ported (B133); Jupiter's has no speed doctrine (B135) and Venus's was withdrawn on a single-point fit (B134). NOT one of the five inputs the scope survey named -- and NOT an input the document withholds either. It is the downstream cost of a decision WE made: STEP4_DECISIONS section 12.10 withdrew the Mars and Venus wheels because each threshold was fitted to ONE crossing and so could not fail. Both groups blocked here would be portable today under the withdrawn thresholds -- every one of silver-bearish#6's thirteen printed rows resolves exactly through B134's Venus wheel -- so this row states what that decision cost, and a year supplying a second crossing is what lifts it

## Where the port disagreed with the scope survey

The survey classed 41 groups READY. Three of them are blocked here on evidence found while writing them, and one group it had not counted was ported. Net 38.

* **`gold-bullish#6`** *If Mars is Aspected by Saturn and Jupiter is Retrograde* — **blocked** on `aspect_orb`. SCOPE SURVEY SAID READY; IT IS NOT. The survey read this as 'a two-body aspect plus the motion field, both already used by catalogue-B rules'. The motion half is right and the aspect half is not: the layer emits `aspect/conjunction` and `aspect/opposition` and no other angle, and this group's own printed row is Saturn in Pisces with Mars in Sagittarius -- the tenth-house graha drishti, which is neither. Blocked on `aspect_orbs`, the open config question whose text is 'graha drishti vs degree orbs', so it is still one of the five and not a sixth.
* **`silver-bullish#10`** *Mercury or Jupiter Do Vedh of Venus* — **blocked** on `vedha_wheel`. SCOPE SURVEY SAID READY; IT IS NOT, and the table says something different again from the heading. The heading's condition is a disjunction and JUPITER's half has no wheel: B135 is blocked on the slow-planet speed doctrine, so only Mercury's half is computable and half a disjunction is not this group. Separately, the two printed rows are VENUS rows -- Venus in Purva Bhadrapad vedhing Punarvasu, 22-Feb-26 00:39 to 04-Mar-26 17:11 -- which is a row of gold-bearish#3's benefic table with Venus as the VEDHER, not Venus being vedhed by anyone. Both facts are recorded; neither is reconciled by us.
* **`silver-bearish#6`** *Mercury Venus or Moon Venus Mutual Vedh* — **blocked** on `vedha_wheel`. SCOPE SURVEY SAID READY; IT IS NOT. Every one of the thirteen printed rows is a VENUS row -- Venus in Dhanistha vedhing Ashlesha, Venus in Chitra vedhing Purva Bhadrapada, and so on -- and each resolves exactly through B134's Venus wheel. B134 is withdrawn: Venus's speed level was fitted to a single 2026 crossing, so the CLASS the wheel is keyed on carries no evidence. The transcription is right and the key is unearned, which is the ruling B134 itself records.
* **`silver-bullish#11`** *Mercury Combust and Retrograde Does Mutual Vedh with Moon* — **ported**, as a resolved ambiguity. The wheel entry used is a transcription of B133's own table and not a derivation; a change to it is a transcription edit. Mumbai only, because the combustion half is date_only at the primary horizon. IT FIRES ZERO TIMES IN 2027 AND THE ZERO HAS THREE CAUSES, which `mercury_vedh_moon_residencies` separates rather than collapsing: Mercury has eight combust-and-retrograde residencies in the generated span; five of them (Dhanishta, Ardra, Mrigashira, Chitra, Shravana) are keys the 2026 table never printed under Retrograde, so there is no target; one (Shatabhisha, 12-17 Feb-2027) has the target ABHIJEET, the 28th nakshatra, which `nakshatra_scheme: 27` does not emit -- the Moon can never be found in it, so that residency is blocked rather than absent; and one (Swati, 9-15 Oct-2027, target Rohini) is fully computable and the Moon was not in Rohini during it. Only the last is a statement about the sky.

## Ported but never firing in 2027

12 of the 38. Surfaced rather than tolerated: a rule that never fires is either correct or a porting error and the two look identical from outside. Each is pinned by name with its reason in `tests/test_rule_layer.py::test_configuration_zero_firings_are_each_the_kind_they_claim`, so a thirteenth appearing fails the harness.

* `gold-bullish#1` — When Mars Passes Through Taurus
* `gold-bullish#4` — Jupiter Enters Gemini
* `gold-bullish#12` — Mars in Pushya Nakshtra
* `silver-bullish#9` — Sun and Moon Together on Sankranti Entering Time
* `silver-bullish#11` — Mercury Combust and Retrograde Does Mutual Vedh with Moon
* `silver-bullish#12` — Venus Combust in West — Bullish Till It Rises in East
* `silver-bullish#19` — Mars Rising — Bullish in Short Term
* `silver-bullish#20` — Saturn and Neptune Conjunction
* `silver-bearish#4` — Mars Vargottam in Cancer
* `sugar-bullish#4` — Moon Joins Combust Mercury in West
* `sugar-bullish#5` — Retrograde Mercury If Goes Combust in Cancer
* `sugar-bearish#1` — Jupiter in Hast or Shravan Nakshtra or Mars in Dhanistha

## What this port does NOT do

* It does not put a configuration row in `build/calendar_2027.*`. `verdicts.py` fires catalogue B alone, and porting a group is not publishing it. The calendar's own apparatus panel says so.
* It does not raise a confidence or emit a verdict record. `label_scheme_signoff` is still open.
* It does not settle any of the six missing inputs.

Financial astrology is a speculative interpretive framework. Nothing on this page is a forecast or investment advice.
